text: A summer at age five felt like it lasted forever.
Whoa, another year's already gone. Why does it go by so fast now?
Turns out, this explanation is a pretty old idea - over a century old. People back then apparently felt the same thing.
Your brain judges how long a year feels by comparing it to your whole life so far.
That gap just keeps widening - at five, at twenty, at fifty.
So the more years you've lived, the smaller that same one year starts to feel.
There's also a theory that a year full of new experiences feels longer looking back - or so it's said.
